Tyler the Creator, a controversial US rapper, was recently "banned" from performing in Australia by Australian feminist organization Collective Shout, whom have been trying to get him banned in an intensive campaign ever since his first tour in 2013, on the grounds of inciting violence, rape and misogyny against women. The reason I use quotation marks for the word "banned" is because that's what he claimed in a tweet, Australia has not actually withdrawn his visa, which would mean he has left Australia of his own free will. Here's the most comprehensive and unbiased article I could find. http://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/music/confusion-as-tyler-the-creator-claims-hes-banned-from-australia-20150728-gilx2z.html

Out of curiosity, I decided to read up on some of his songs, and...yeah, I'd put a trigger warning on that, there's some pretty shocking stuff there. The reason I wanted to post this was mainly to see what you feminists and non-feminists thought on the topic. It doesn't appear to be censorship, as Australia has not withdrawn his visa, but Collective Shout was calling for censorship to take place. Were they justified in doing so? Are the lyrics to Tyler's songs so vile that they have to be silenced, or should we take an anti-censorship position and defend his right to say what he says, even if we fundamentally find it distasteful? Personally, I am in favor of the anti-censorship option, and the best response would be to use our freedom of speech to mock the guy with witty memes and satires. What do you guys think?

It all started in Kindergarten in 81-82.

Halfway through the 2nd/3rd week of school, they wheeled in a cart with an Apple ][ with a green-screen monochrome monitor. The only game that they had was a MECC game that had a caterpillar that you helped do letters or numbers (can't remember, have never found it).

I was completely entranced. I'd never seen anything like it. I went home and told my parents we absolutely needed an Apple computer. They blew me off, silly kindergarten son saying he wants one of those stupid new computer things.

I was obsessed. I would play every chance I got. Rocky's Boots was a specifically good one that I liked as I got older.

My obsession got to the point that in 1st-2nd grade during standardized testing, I would fill out random circles to be done first and go play on the computer for the rest of the day. I totally got away with it too - until I had to come clean years later when my scores suddenly amazingly quintupled.

Eventually, my parents caught on that it was important, and decided to buy me a computer. Parents found a classified ad of a guy selling a used computer with software. They bought it for my 8th birthday. I was really shocked - not just because they got me a computer, but because it was a COMMODORE 64.

I was pissed. I wanted an Apple. I didn't know better. After a bit, I found that the C64 had come with a disk drive and about 70 disks. Little did I know that these disks were overflowing with pirated games! (Donkey Kong, Zaxxon, Archon, etc.) Only a few would work out of the box, but I found lots more that wouldn't load. I spent months learning how to get them to work - most just needed to be LOADed, then the right SYS XXXXX code to be ran to start (vs the standard RUN). It was pure elation when I'd get a new game working for the first time. I even found a few porn games.. but that's another story for a later time.

The struggle for gaming and the Apple and C64 were highlights of my childhood. I wish I could recreate the experience for my own kids somehow.
